public_role: Owner / utility licensor for CSX corridors
online_system: CSX Property Portal (external users register as CSX Customer); case dashboard, notes, uploads, status tracking, agreement distribution; separate Outside Party request for construction scheduling.
published_standard_clock: Average about 30 days for CSX review; not a guaranteed completion SLA. Acknowledgement/invoice and estimated review time are sent after receipt. Variance, site assessment, incomplete package and third-party/internal review add time.
published_expedite: $7,500 surcharge plus normal review/license charges; target 15 working days to agreement for individually pre-approved eligible cases. Published stage targets: receipt confirmation 1 business day; initial engineering review 5 business days; applicant revision due 3 business days; one re-review 2 business days; contract preparation 4 business days.
key_exclusions: No expedite for spec deviations, shortline-leased track, rights-of-entry, bridge/MOW/public-project signoffs, drainage or casing over 36 in; expedite does not schedule flagging/construction.
published_base_cost: Per location: underground casing <10 in $1,910 standard / $4,420 variance; higher casing sizes cost more. Add agreement/license, RPL/insurance, protection, signal locate, construction management and possible extra review costs.

public_role: NS pipe/wire application manager and engineering/agreement processor
online_system: NS RailPros Permit Management Portal: register account; pipe/wire application; attachments; messages; real-time status; agreement execution; fee payment; field service coordination.
published_standard_clock: No standard end-to-end review duration located in public NS pipe/wire program pages. RailPros states processing starts only after complete form, engineered plan/profile, scope, prior agreement if applicable and fee are received.
published_expedite: Published portal procedure: plan review target 2 business days; draft agreement target 3 business days after engineering approval; fully executed agreement target 4 business days after applicant execution and delivery of required insurance/fees. Revisions, variance, bridge review and excluded occupancy types are outside these stage clocks.
key_exclusions: Check current portal procedure for eligibility; expedited handling is not a blanket end-to-end SLA. Construction still requires license, written proceed authorization and scheduling of flagging/monitoring.
published_base_cost: Underground wireline application $2,250; expedited underground wireline $8,000 additional; variance $3,500; additional reviews after first two $500 each. License, insurance/RPL or risk fee, flagging, inspection/monitoring and other services are extra.

public_role: UP property owner / permanent utility license signatory for Chicago CJR territory
online_system: UP online Utilities Installations application. Select wireline crossing, encroachment, modification or maintenance; distinguish crossing (enters and exits ROW) from encroachment (longitudinal/does not exit). Use combined crossing+encroachment classification if both apply.
published_standard_clock: Wireline crossing agreement processing approximately 30–45 days after a complete conforming online application. License fee based on property value is provided after review/approval. Agreements must be executed before work; verbal authorization is not allowed.
published_expedite: Tier I $12,055 / 5 UP business days; Tier II $6,055 / 15 UP business days. Only crossing applications; combined crossing+encroachment, encroachments, deviations from standards, and pipeline crossings over 40 in cannot be rushed. Published turnaround is for application handling, not construction access or field scheduling.
key_exclusions: Survey entry is separate temporary ROE if needed. A crossing that also occupies ROW longitudinally must follow both processes and cannot use rush handling. Coordinate CJR operations separately because UP owns property but CJR operates the short line.
published_base_cost: No standard fee stated online for license: property-value based, set after review. Add insurance/RPL, license rent, flagging/signal protection and CJR operating/entry charges as applicable.

public_role: CJR is the local operator; UP owns the Centex/Elk Grove rail property
online_system: CJR railroad page links to Progressive Rail Jotform Right of Entry “info/permit request.” Form captures requestor/contractor/billing, work type, location, milepost and coordinates. Treat it as a request/intake and temporary-access workflow; UP’s online Utilities application remains the permanent property license path.
published_standard_clock: Jotform states allow up to 3–5 business days for processing. It does not promise a fully executed permanent utility license or construction release in that time. Public CJR materials reviewed did not publish a separate utility crossing review SLA, utility fee schedule or agreement lifecycle.
published_expedite: No CJR-specific expedite tier or published permanent-license SLA found in public sources. After intake, expect further instructions/packet; obtain CJR operations concurrence, track access, signal/utility locate, flagging/monitoring and any CJR-specific agreement requirements.
key_exclusions: A CJR Right of Entry request does not replace UP property approval. Progressive Rail generic/facility-entry terms are not proof of the CJR construction terms; do not import rates or insurance requirements from another PGR railroad/location.
published_base_cost: CJR-specific permanent wireline application/license fees, insurance, flagging and inspection/monitoring pricing not publicly established in sources reviewed; request a written estimate through the form/contact after submitting a complete location packet.
